alpha_why: alpha in mission_scoring.combine_with_similarity: final = alpha * similarity_pct + (1 - alpha) * suitability. 0.5 is that function's own default (mission_scoring.py line 207). Adopting the library default is still a decision on an open question (how much lunar likeness against mission fitness), so it is pending team confirmation; ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3 gives the effect of 0.3 and 0.7 on each mission's top 10.

funnel.name: common gates
funnel.text: Common hard filters of every mission: elevation_m >= 1.0 (Earth only); mask_fraction >= 0.3 (both bodies). Failing one eliminates the cell for the mission.

funnel.name: required variables
funnel.text: Every variable in the mission's require_present list must have a value; a missing one eliminates the cell with the reason '<variable> no data'.

funnel.name: mission hard filters
funnel.text: The mission's own gates (missions[].gates, with their limits); failing one eliminates the cell for that mission (no score, no rank), with the exact reason, e.g. '<variable> outside [<min>, <max>]'. An eliminated cell may still pass another mission.

funnel.name: suitability
funnel.text: Survivors only: suitability = 100 * sum(w * u) / sum(w over weighted variables with a value); utility u runs linearly from 0 at 'bad' to 1 at 'good', clipped (tables for classes); contribution = w * u; a missing weighted variable is ignored and the remaining weights renormalised; coverage = weight with a value / total weight.

funnel.name: similarity
funnel.text: rover, solar: similarity on real values (similarity.json real_value): per variable s = exp(-0.5 * (|earth - moon| / tolerance)^2), similarity = 100 * weighted mean of s; the twin is the lunar zone cell with every key variable within 1 x its tolerance and every secondary within 2 x its tolerance that has the highest similarity; a point with no such cell has no twin, no similarity and no final (it keeps its suitability). lunar_base: similarity on thermal position and real terrain (missions.json similarity, rule percentile_and_real_tolerance): the variables with scale 'percentile_within_population' are compared as their percentile within their own population (Earth: the points passing the mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of the zone), the others in real values; per variable s = exp(-0.5 * (difference / tolerance)^2), similarity = 100 * weighted mean of s; the twin is the zone cell with every key variable within 1 x its tolerance and every secondary within 2 x its tolerance that has the highest similarity; a point with no such cell has no twin, no similarity and no final (it keeps its suitability). A likeness of position, not of equal values: the real values are shown with every pair.

funnel.name: final
funnel.text: final = alpha * similarity + (1 - alpha) * suitability (alpha in missions.json 'alpha'); survivors with a similarity are ranked by the published final, ties by Earth cell id; survivors without a twin (real-value missions) follow, by published suitability, ties by Earth cell id.

elimination_line_rule: the cell's reason codes (fail_bits) in bit order, their 'text' joined with '; '

known_limitations: The rover thresholds (slope 0.5-15 deg, roughness 5-650 m) were written for a 300 m baseline and are applied unchanged to km-baseline values (slope over about 3.7-3.8 km, roughness at a lag of about 1.9 km; true_baseline in variables.json). km-baseline slopes are much gentler than rover-scale slopes and km-lag roughness is larger than 300 m roughness, so passing these gates says nothing about rover-scale hazards. Nothing was adjusted (known limitation, pending Robotics 1).

Similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning; missions.json similarity): the twin is the cell of the lunar south-polar zone (75-90 S) whose slope is within 2 deg and roughness within 30 m of the Earth cell (illustrative team values of rover_preset.py for a 5 km baseline) and whose relative elevation is within 1,000 m (twice 500 m), with the highest similarity. A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score (missions.json similarity.unpaired_reasons).

Temperature, diurnal amplitude and irradiance are not part of the rover similarity: their values on both sides and the difference are shown for information (the lunar south-polar twins are colder than their Earth points by a median of about 150 K).
The soft criteria have no surface-type term: polar deserts, ice-free Arctic plateaus and steppe score alike when bare and smooth at the km scale.

zone.name: Mare Tranquillitatis & Equatorial Maria
zone.why: Team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning): the equatorial maria as analog_finder defines them (absolute latitude <= 30 degrees and elevation <= -1,200 m), applied to the real lunar table.

similarity.list_rule: paired points by rank, then the points without a twin by published suitability descending, ties by Earth cell id (earth_<mission>_pairs.bin list_order)

known_limitations: The solar twin is matched on sunlight above the atmosphere (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning): Earth's annual-mean sunlight at the top of the atmosphere (DERIVED from latitude) against the lunar surface irradiance of the equatorial maria (|lat| <= 30 deg, elevation <= -1,200 m), within 0.6 kWh/m2/day, with slope and roughness as secondary criteria. Only part of that sunlight reaches the ground on Earth (shown per pair); on the Moon all of it does, in a lunar day of 29.5 Earth days. The maria receive the sunlight of Earth's tropics, so only points within about 33.5 deg of the equator find a twin; the others keep their suitability with no twin (missions.json similarity.unpaired_reasons).

Earth irradiance at the ground, sun geometry and the diurnal amplitude are suitability criteria. Earth irradiance at the ground is surface solar energy under the atmosphere and clouds (WorldClim) and lunar irradiance is airless geometry; the solar gates on irradiance, maximum sun elevation and low-sun fraction remove every lunar cell poleward of facts.moon_pass_abs_lat_max (shown in the lunar fail bits only: lunar cells are not filtered for the similarity).

Temperature and diurnal amplitude are not part of the solar similarity: their values on both sides and the difference are shown for information. 6,060 passing solar cells (all in Antarctica) have no land surface temperature: the amplitude weight drops out of their suitability with the remaining weights renormalised. None of them has a lunar twin (they lie at 64.5 S or further south, far from the latitudes whose sunlight matches the maria), so they have no similarity, no final score and no confidence.

known_limitations: lunar_base is an exact copy of the team's thermal block (team design values, no external source). The ice block is shown per Earth cell as information only (passes or not, its suitability) and never changes this ranking; no lunar cell passes ice because lunar permafrost_class is the MODELLED label 'ninguno', which the ice gate excludes.

Similarity is a likeness of thermal POSITION and real terrain, not of temperature (team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET; missions.json similarity, rule percentile_and_real_tolerance): the coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as percentiles within each population (Earth: the points passing this mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole), each within 10 percentile points, and slope and roughness in real values (within 4 deg and 60 m). Equal positions do not mean equal temperatures: on every pair the twin is far colder and swings far more than the Earth point, and the real values and differences are shown with every pair (similarity.json texts.lunar_base_pair_sentence). A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score (missions.json similarity.unpaired_by_kind).

The coldest temperature (tmin_c) is a MODELLED air temperature on Earth (WorldClim, coldest month, interpolated) and a MEASURED surface temperature on the Moon (Diviner night minimum); the Earth diurnal amplitude is a difference between two satellite overpasses and understates the daily range. Both are suitability criteria on Earth, and in the similarity only their position within each population is compared, never their values.
Antarctica has no land surface temperature product here, so its cells fail on lst_diurnal_amp_k with 'no data' (missing_data).
